dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real matrix A, real vector x, and row i, LocalDef001(A,x,i) = sum over j in Fin n of |A(i,j)| |x(j)|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the final error contribution u sum_j |A(i,j)| |x(j)| and is also nested inside LocalDef002 to measure the magnitude propagation of Ainv applied to q.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef002(A,Ainv,q,i) = sum over j in Fin n of |A(i,j)| LocalDef001(Ainv,q,j) = sum_j |A(i,j)| sum_k |Ainv(j,k)| |q(k)|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the nonnegative quantity multiplied by u in the middle term of the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real matrix A and vector x, LocalDef003(A,x,i) = sum over j in Fin n of A(i,j)x(j), the i-th coordinate of the matrix-vector product Ax.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines Ainv q in the update and rounding hypotheses, A(Ainv q) in the inverse-action hypothesis, and A(xNext-x) on the left-hand side of the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Eq(a,b) is exact propositional equality between two terms of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes both the inverse-action relation and the update formula exact equalities, rather than approximate relations.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite index type with n elements, conventionally represented by the natural indices 0 through n-1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes all matrices to n by n dimensions, all vectors to dimension n, and all coordinate quantifiers and sums to the same finite index set.

dependency_coverage.meaning: HAdd.hAdd selects the binary addition operation supplied by an HAdd instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied real instances, every occurrence is ordinary real addition in the update formula and in the right-hand sides of the bounds.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: HMul.hMul selects the binary multiplication operation supplied by an HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied real instances, it is ordinary real multiplication in matrix-vector products, weighted sums, and the terms multiplied by u.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: HSub.hSub selects the binary subtraction operation supplied by an HSub instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied real instance, it forms the coordinatewise real difference xNext(j)-x(j) inside A(xNext-x).

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: LE.le selects the less-than-or-equal relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real order instance, it expresses 0 <= u and both componentwise absolute-value bounds.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Nat is the type of natural numbers, including zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The universally quantified natural number n determines the common matrix and vector dimension and permits the zero-dimensional case.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: OfNat.ofNat interprets a natural-number literal in a type having the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with the real zero instances, it interprets the literal 0 in the hypothesis 0 <= u as the real number zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real is the scalar type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Every matrix entry, vector coordinate, scalar u, arithmetic expression, absolute value, and inequality in the proposition is real-valued.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instAdd equips the real numbers with their ordinary addition operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the additions in xNext(i) = (Ainv q)(i) + x(i) + h(i) and in the right-hand sides of the inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instAddGroup supplies the additive-group structure of the real numbers, including additive inverses.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is used by the definition of absolute value and supports the ordinary signed real arithmetic appearing in the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instLE equips the real numbers with their ordinary less-than-or-equal relation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the standard meanings of nonnegativity and of all stated upper bounds.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instMul equips the real numbers with their ordinary multiplication operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines all products in the matrix-vector sums, absolute-value majorants, and factors involving u.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instSub defines real subtraction by a-b = a+(-b).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the ordinary coordinatewise difference xNext(j)-x(j) used in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instZero supplies the ordinary real number zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides the lower endpoint in 0 <= u and the additive identity underlying empty finite sums.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.lattice supplies the lattice operations associated with the usual order on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It allows abs(a) to be defined as max(a,-a), hence as the ordinary real absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: Zero.toOfNat0 converts a Zero instance into an OfNat instance for the numeral 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures that the numeral in the hypothesis 0 <= u denotes the real additive identity.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an ordered additive group, abs(a) is max(a,-a); on the real numbers this is the ordinary absolute value |a|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It measures the componentwise magnitudes of h, Ainv q, x, q, A(xNext-x), and all matrix entries and vector coordinates inside LocalDef001 and LocalDef002.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: instHAdd converts a homogeneous Add operation on a type into the corresponding homogeneous HAdd operation.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin.fintype(n) supplies a finite enumeration of all elements of Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the universal finite index set available to the sums defining LocalDef001, LocalDef002, and LocalDef003.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: Finset.sum(s,f) is the additive sum of f over the finite set s.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives all matrix-vector and absolute-value majorant expressions their finite-sum meanings.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: Finset.univ is the finite set containing every element of a finite type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Fin n, it makes each local definition sum over every coordinate j from 0 through n-1.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instAddCommMonoid supplies the commutative additive-monoid structure of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides the associative, commutative real addition and zero required to define all finite sums, including an empty sum as zero.

binders: n is an arbitrary natural number, possibly zero.
A and Ainv are arbitrary real n by n matrices, represented as functions Fin n -> Fin n -> Real.
x, q, h, and xNext are arbitrary real vectors of dimension n, represented as functions Fin n -> Real.
u is an arbitrary real scalar.
The conclusion is universally quantified over each coordinate i in Fin n; the hypotheses containing an index are likewise required at every coordinate.
There are no existentially quantified witnesses.
hypotheses: Ainv acts as a right inverse of A on the particular vector q: for every i, sum_j A(i,j)(sum_k Ainv(j,k)q(k)) = q(i).
The next vector satisfies the exact componentwise update xNext(i) = (sum_j Ainv(i,j)q(j)) + x(i) + h(i) for every i.
The perturbation h satisfies the componentwise bound |h(i)| <= u |sum_j Ainv(i,j)q(j)| + u |x(i)| for every i.
conclusions: For every i in Fin n, |sum_j A(i,j)(xNext(j)-x(j))| <= |q(i)| + u sum_j |A(i,j)| sum_k |Ainv(j,k)| |q(k)| + u sum_j |A(i,j)| |x(j)|.
mathematical_definitions: All sums indexed by j or k range over Fin n; an empty sum is zero.
For any matrix M and vector v, (Mv)(i) = sum_j M(i,j)v(j).
The vector xNext-x is formed coordinatewise: (xNext-x)(j) = xNext(j)-x(j).
Every absolute value is the ordinary real absolute value; no vector or matrix norm occurs.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every dimension n, real matrices A and Ainv, real vectors x, q, h, and xNext, and nonnegative real u, suppose that A(Ainv q) equals q exactly, that xNext = Ainv q + x + h componentwise, and that each |h(i)| is at most u times |(Ainv q)(i)| plus u times |x(i)|. Then, at every coordinate i, the absolute value of the i-th coordinate of A(xNext-x) is at most |q(i)| plus u times sum_j |A(i,j)| sum_k |Ainv(j,k)| |q(k)| plus u times sum_j |A(i,j)| |x(j)|.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Ainv is not required to be an inverse of A as a matrix. The only encoded relation is A(Ainv q) = q for the single supplied vector q.
The statement imposes no invertibility, nonsingularity, rank, symmetry, or dimensional positivity condition on A or Ainv.
The scalar u is required only to be nonnegative; no upper bound such as u < 1 is encoded.
For a negative u, the antecedent 0 <= u is false, so the corresponding implication is vacuously true.
When n = 0, Fin n is empty, all coordinatewise hypotheses and the conclusion are vacuous, and the proposition carries no matrix or vector content.
As an implication, the proposition is also vacuously true whenever any required inverse-action, update, or rounding hypothesis is not satisfied.
The conclusion bounds |A(xNext-x)| componentwise. It does not bound a residual such as |A(xNext-x)-q|.
The quantities are exact real numbers. No floating-point type, rounding operation, computed-value predicate, or operational evaluation model is encoded.
The error estimates use entrywise absolute values and finite weighted sums, not a vector norm or induced matrix norm.
The vectors q, x, h, and xNext have no restrictions beyond the displayed hypotheses.
